Senses.Explanation: Ten thousand miles without an inch of grass. Dongshan Liangjie, pressed by Huayan's honest admitting that he has no reasoning-path, rules that just so he must go to the grassless ten thousand miles — and when Huayan asks whether he may go there, seals it: just so, go; Yuanwu Keqin closes his retreat-dissolving verse on it — ninety days' work complete, no need to test the wax man, and yet though the ten thousand miles hold no inch of grass, the bag's mouth opens today; Wuzhun Shifan lists the ancients' moves at the retreat's end and tears them all off at once — Cuiyan's talking east and west, Yangshan's millet fields, Wenyuan's fall into donkey dung, Dongshan's trailing his heel toward the grassless ten thousand miles; Wansong Xingxiu opens his own hall instruction by pairing it — the grassless ten thousand miles: clean ground deludes people; eight directions without a wisp of cloud: clear sky cheats you. Gulin Qingmao, having opened the ancients' sky-road and named it the great pure extinction, licenses the assembly to go east or west at tomorrow's Pravarana — only not to the grassless ten thousand miles; Luyan He, after raising Dongshan's charge, Shishuang's grass-at-the-door and Ming'an's grass-even-inside, rules the formula only says half — out the door or in, they are all men in the grass — and demands the turning-around phrase; Liaozong Chaojian judges the three old men one nostril breathing, themselves standing in the grass, then answers his own question — through the bramble thicket, not one leaf wet; and Yushan Shangsi warns that to go to the grassless ten thousand miles leaves dead men beyond count on flat ground, while to hide where grass begins at the door takes a good hand threading the brambles — the true performer poles open a line wherever he lands.

Entries.SourceTerm: 萬里無寸草，出門便是草

Senses.PreferredTarget: Ten thousand miles without a blade of grass; step outside and it is grass already
AlternateTargets: No grass for ten thousand miles; beyond the door, grass everywhere
SearchAliases: ten thousand miles without grass step outside and it is grass already
Senses.Note: The paired line joins two old replies: Dongshan sends his assembly toward a place without a blade of grass for ten thousand miles, while Shishuang says that stepping outside is already grass. Later masters combine those opposing images to challenge the wish for a pure place beyond everyday circumstances. Their fresh verses and talks use the line at the close of retreat, for travel, and as a test of where one stands.

Senses.Explanation: "Ten thousand miles without a blade of grass; step outside and it is grass already" places a grassless ideal beside the ground met at the door. Xisou writes a travel verse on the old exchange, and Xiaoyin takes up the paired line when ending summer retreat. Jieshi rejects resting in either side, Pingshi answers with a common road, and Gulin turns the two old replies into a verse.

Senses.Explanation: The grassless place of ten thousand miles. Because the headword is the destination inside Dongshan's close-of-retreat charge, most windows carry it in the quoted case; the retained witnesses are the masters whose own turns deploy the exchange. Dahui Zonggao, recalling how the whole age's answers failed the charge and Shishuang's grass-at-the-door won Dongshan's Liuyang-ancient-buddha praise, supplies the analysis in his own voice: Dongshan's order to the grassless place is the question on the principle side — answer it there with dead words and it dies on one side — which is why Shishuang answered on the fact side. Hongzhi Zhengjue, raising the charge and its two answers, rules on the whole exchange: out the door is grass — one wades the thick-springing tangle, leaves falling to announce autumn, dropping into the dark green — and here one must catch the mechanism where the lock turns but the seal is not yet formed. Shiyu Mingfang stacks all three old lines — the grassless destination, the grass at the door, the grass even indoors — and rules they leave you no move at all, only because you cannot walk among the other-kind; then counts on his fingers chicken, dog, pig, goat, ox, horse — and asks why the seventh, human, goes unsaid. And Binya Jian, having raised the same triple, types the three old men like smugglers: one an eagle-hearted goose-clawed type who can say it but not do it, one a tiger-faced bear-livered type who can do it but not say it, one lying in the bramble thicket with no hope of standing up. Shenfeng Xian, at his own summer's close, turns the charge against the assembly: brambles cover the ground under your heels — to set out for the grassless ten thousand miles is very hard, very hard; wear out pairs of straw sandals and you still never leave this spot — better to keep to one's original portion. Lianfeng Su, raising the three worthies, rules they plucked one blade of grass out of a clean white ground and tripped up countless wandering monks — so he, seeing injustice on the road, pokes one spark from the stove to burn the blade and spare the dharma-hall a deeper grass. Chulin Shangrui, after the charge, the door-grass and Dongshan's how-many-in-the-great-Tang cry, answers the whole thing in verse: the grassless ten thousand miles — in the vast universe, travelers are few; out the door it is grass — falling flowers, flowing water, birds crying; the imperial way shows its honor without favor, and the drum-bellied singers of its peace have grown old. And Miyun Yuanwu, raising the charge at his own retreat's end, refuses it with replacement: Yumen today does not ask east-going or west-going — go to where withered wood flowers, go to where the icy river flames — then snatches up the staff: when you meet someone, by all means do not miss the mark; throws the staff, shouts, and descends.

Entries.SourceTerm: 萬里無雲，青天也須喫棒

Senses.PreferredTarget: For ten thousand miles there is no cloud, yet even the blue sky deserves a blow.
Senses.Note: A blow is due even when the sky appears perfectly clear; no pure state is exempt from testing. Some witnesses cite the line as old speech; the retained sources each apply it within a current teaching turn.

Senses.Explanation: For ten thousand miles there is no cloud, yet even the blue sky deserves a blow. A blow is due even when the sky appears perfectly clear; no pure state is exempt from testing. The source-backed uses include Sanyi Mingyu in J27nB189, Yikui Yuankui in J37nB388, Tianran Hanshi in J38nB406, and Baichi Xingyuan in J28nB202. Each is a current use of the full line. The image keeps its paired structure across the records. Some witnesses cite the line as old speech; the retained sources each apply it within a current teaching turn.

Senses.Explanation: The first phrase names the first position in a numbered sequence, not a single sentence shared by every record. Yuanwu Keqin sets it beside a second and third phrase in a hall address. An unnamed monk asks Nanyuan Huiyong how to state the first phrase, while Hanyue Fazang supplies contrasted first-, second-, and third-phrase lines. The differing answers show that “first” selects a slot in a verbal arrangement.

Entries.SourceTerm: 第一句中薦得，堪與佛祖為師

Senses.PreferredTarget: If you discern it in the first phrase, you can be a teacher to buddhas and ancestors
SearchAliases: if you discern it in the first phrase, you can be a teacher to buddhas and ancestors
Senses.Note: Linji says that one who discerns the first phrase could teach buddhas and ancestors. Feiyin quotes the full threefold ranking and turns its results upside down. Qianyan invokes the first phrase to urge listeners to look back into their own situation. Xingkong composes a verse for each of the three ranks, and Tianru asks how Linji’s daring formula sits beside the answers he later gave a monk. The line is a challenge to discernment, not a certificate earned by repeating a phrase.

Entries.SourceTerm: 第一句薦得，堪與佛祖為師

Senses.PreferredTarget: Recognize the first phrase, and you can teach Buddhas and ancestors
SearchAliases: recognize the first phrase, and you can teach buddhas and ancestors
Senses.Note: The first of Linji’s three phrases says that one who recognizes it can teach Buddhas and ancestors; the second and third mark lesser degrees of recognition. Tian’an voices the sequence on New Year’s Day and asks what the first phrase is before offering a seasonal line. Boshan explicitly cites Linji, then says he would give a blow to someone claiming recognition of the first phrase. Yuan’an asks his assembly which phrase they have recognized and probes their replies. Chulin treats the threefold ranking as compassionate, provisional speech and replaces each tier with a criticism. These uses keep the apparent hierarchy from hardening into a certificate of attainment.

Senses.Explanation: “The head seat” names the senior monastic office or, by metonymy, the head-seat officeholder. Eight independent recorded-sayings and master-commentary works show appointment to the office, succession, preaching duties, and explicit comparison with the second seat. These predicates establish the office-and-officeholder sense. Literal ordinal uses, such as an empty foremost place or the first group in a seating order, are a separate contextual use and do not establish the monastic office. In the Nanquan construction, institutional parallels support “Nanquan’s head seat” or “the head-seat officeholder at Nanquan.” The grammar can permit “Nanquan, then head seat” in an explicit biography, but the phrase alone does not establish that exceptional reading.

Senses.Explanation: The first-principle truth. Tianran Hanshi grades the four standings at his own birthday feast — keeping worldly truth only is commoner dharma, leaving it for another truth is śrāvaka dharma, worldly truth itself being this truth is bodhisattva dharma, and neither, with the mind free to aim, is tathāgata dharma; Feiyin Tongrong answers the gavel-master's opening line at his Tian童 inauguration saying this truth was forged by the very first hammer-blow, Linye Tongqi says of it that it had already been proclaimed in full before the gavel fell, and Zhuanyu Guanheng writes to a patron that the father-son reunion at home is the first joy of the human world, is itself this truth, is itself unsurpassed great nirvana. Shanyi Ruchun calls the very project of observing it a hole dug in empty space and a wound cut in good flesh, Zhangxue Tongzui finds every phrase of street-quarter small talk illumining it while Guanyin comes buying with cash, Yi'an Shanzan tells the assembly it need not be sought elsewhere, Yulin Tongxu stands up at the New Year hall to hold it out in the open and then calls everyone to rise at the meal-drum and recite the Amitāyus Buddha, Lianyue Daozheng reads his enthronement proclamation so that tortoise-lines and horse-charts, dragon-script and phoenix-brilliance each fully display it, and Zhe'an Jingfan, after raising Śākyamuni's promise to disclose it, says it was never once touched — porridge at porridge-time, rice at rice-time — and that it does not deceive.

Senses.Explanation: The second phrase marks a middle position in a locally numbered sequence of Chan sayings; its specific content changes with the exchange. Sanfeng and Jiqi supply older verse and case uses. Tianan sets it beside first and third levels, Chaozong, Pinjixiang, and Lingyin answer current questions about it, and Yuanjie calls his own staff demonstration the second phrase. Senses.PreferredTarget: Grasp the second phrase and you may teach humans and devas
SearchAliases: grasp the second phrase and you may teach humans and devas
Senses.Note: Linji ranks three kinds of recognition: the second phrase makes one fit to teach humans and devas. Boshan repeats the ranking, then says grasping the second phrase adds fetters rather than authority. Jiqi repeats it and answers the middle phrase by urging the listener to carry it out and see. Xingkong says splitting one matter into three misleads people; Heyi quotes the same line and challenges his audience to show which phrase they have grasped. The expression is a benchmark that each later teacher tests rather than a certificate earned by repeating it.

Senses.Explanation: A second moon is an apparent duplicate: visible or asserted beside the first, but not a second lunar object established in its own right. Masters challenge claims that add another position by asking which moon it is, call even refined sayings a second moon, and contrast first and second in direct questions; explanatory records also list it with reflections and optical appearances. Senses.Explanation: The eighth consciousness is the numbered field in which Dahui says a lifetime's deeds are stored. Chushi says the ancestral blade cuts there; Yuansou warns that taking its bright, responsive activity for one's own host mistakes the beginningless karmic-consciousness mass for what is real. Dahui connects the stored deeds to the habitual attractions that seize a person when body and elements disperse. Chushi contrasts the ancestral sayings with conceptual calculation and says the blade cuts directly at the eighth consciousness. Yuansou names a tempting inference from speech and lucid awareness, then rejects it as the root of birth and death.

Entries.SourceTerm: 般若如大火聚，近之則燎卻面門

Senses.PreferredTarget: Prajna is like a great mass of fire; approach it and your face is scorched
AlternateTargets: Wisdom is a great fire: come near and it burns your face
SearchAliases: prajna great fire approach scorches face
Senses.Note: The saying likens prajna to a great mass of fire: approach carelessly and it burns your face. Shiqi uses it to halt deliberation before direct responsibility. Lianyue voices it while drawing a circle with his staff and calling his assembly into the furnace. Xiuye puts it against calculating thought, Yikui warns against clinging to an easy phrase, and Wanfeng invokes it against settling into a blank view. The fire image marks the danger of treating insight as a manageable object.

Occurrences.Kwic: 得法自在，布褌上提持，名喧宇宙。山僧庶事無能，安踵前賢之轍？雖然如是，更有諸佛說不到、祖師拈不出底句在。且道是那一句？」以拄杖指云：「淵泉涌玉常盈座，峻嶺堆藍欲接天。」開爐，上堂。師云：「鉗鎚惡辣祖師機，好手何妨盡力揮？若遇銅頭鐵額漢，頂門一擊火星飛。眾中有當爐不避火者，請出來互相擎展。」僧問：「九夏已去，三冬復臨，如何是和尚作用？」師云：「只是現成。」進云：「如何是現成句？」師云：「坐蠟玉泉池更冷，開爐松火焰彌高。」僧禮拜，師乃云：「般若如大火聚，近之則燎卻面門。」以拄杖打圓相，云：「山僧即以般若為爐，汝等諸人全身在箇中同經鍛煉。且道一鎚便就時如何發用？巨冶紅爐成利器，管教觸處露鋒鋩。」以拄杖拍禪床，下座。上堂。僧問：「南有曹谿，北有玉泉，兩處宗風，是同？是別？」師云：「同則總同，別則總別。」進云：「同別且置，如何是菩提樹？」師云：「何似斫倒？」進云：「如何是明鏡臺？」師云：「何似踢倒？」進云：「因甚秀祖道有，六祖道無？」師云：「何似兩頭坐斷？」進云：「今日和尚據款結案去也。」師便喝一喝，僧禮

Occurrences.Kwic: 世尊在法華會上盡力只道箇『是法非思量分別之所能解』。此是釋迦老子開方便、顯實相之包括也。誌公和尚云：『內外追尋覓總無，境上施為渾大有。』昔雪峰存禪師亦為此事不明，三登投子、九到洞山，尚機緣不契。後參德山鑒禪師，造室中問：『從上宗風以何法示人？』德山云：『我宗無語句，亦無一法與人。』後又問：『從上宗乘中事，學人還有分也無？』德山拈拄杖打云：『道甚麼？』雪峰於時撞破漆桶。諸禪德！以此諦觀，計較心思，靈利聰明，此箇門中一點也用不著。所以云：『般若如大火聚，近之則燎卻面門。』擬思躊躇，便落意識。者裏唯證者方知；若未證者，直須證取，方名真正出家兒。若心不正，心外取證，是名出家外道，不堪為種草。永嘉大師云：『損法財、滅功德，莫不由此心意識。』是故心意識乃障道業，亦使人七顛八倒，儘在外邊走，為諸不善。䜋則還源達本，不逐其末，但得本，其末自至。眾禪德！既有窮究此道之心，誠欲立堅固志，挺身勇猛直前，不至大休、大歇、大解脫處誓不退墮。驀然向心思意解計較不及處，見徹父母未生面孔，即是伊脫生死放身命處也。久立，珍重！」

Occurrences.Kwic: 木，見人東說東、西說西，影響音聞，是從無量劫來一齊翻出的。故爾隨處作主，遇緣即宗，左逢右遇，能大能小，皆以海印三昧一印印定現量一著子。先聖得此印，所以不起滅定現諸威儀，不捨道法示凡夫相，拈香撥火、運水搬柴，何曾障著些子？風行空而舟御水，脫脫洒洒，豈不快哉？到這裏，正永嘉所謂：「亦無人，亦無佛，大千沙界海中漚，一切聖賢如電拂，非是強為法如是。」故莫看前輩如是說話，坐在無事界中，一切落空又不是也。須知當人親證之時，直下求空了不可得，故曰：「般若如大火聚，近之則燎卻面門；如喻太末蟲，處處能泊而不能泊於火焰之上。」旨哉言乎！近代佛法可傷，為師者既道眼不明，學者又為聲色所扇，且不問撥艸瞻風畢竟為著何事，徒快一時，從此一盲眾盲沿之不息，轉相授受而正宗微矣。玉甫居士遍參諸方二十餘年，康熙丙辰見汶叟於晴川，從前所學盡形披露，汶叟亦不肯以近代息氣相待，一味以本分期之，雖向上眼未開而腳跟已正，因緣到來自是不差。我又觀之，居士如已成之龍，只次點眼，藥信若發，何怕你不掣天飛去？則山僧所說都是剩語也。示彭君甫居士六十法語

Senses.Explanation: Scripture, verse, address, and liturgy passages retain the named perfection of wisdom. The shorter expression stays one named perfection across its several voice layers. The “great perfection of wisdom” expression is the counted expanded form and is linked as such.

Senses.PreferredTarget: Wisdom does not grasp at knowing, yet nothing is left unknown
AlternateTargets: Prajna knows nothing, and there is nothing it does not know
Senses.Note: The paired saying gives wisdom without grasping knowledge and yet without a gap in knowing. Yezhu says ‘without knowing’ must not be mistaken for simple ignorance. Cishou pairs the line with ‘without seeing, nothing unseen’ and tests it against an old question on wisdom's body and use. Hanyue and Yuanjie have verses in their collections under this heading; the headings do not prove they coined the saying.

Occurrences.Kwic: 衣中寶，無明醉自醒。百骸俱潰散，一物鎮長靈。遂拈拄杖云：拄杖子不可靈也。又舉拂子云：拂子不可靈也。諸仁者，如今百骸未散、六根完具時，便要認得箇靈底一物。諸人若無此物，十二時中將什麼拈匙把筯及動轉施為？諸人若無此物，即今將什麼聞法？臨際喚做無位真人，六祖呼為本來面目，石頭名為菴中不死人，洞山指作家中不老者。譬如大海之水通貫百川，在江曰江水，在河曰河水，及到通宗會源處、雲霞消散時，又且喚做什麼？要知端的□，問取虗空。顧大夫為妻懷□，請上堂。般若無知，無所不知；般若無見，無所不見。無知之知，是為真知；無見之見，是為真見。昔僧問智門：如何是般若體？門云：蚌含明月。又問：如何是般若用？門云：兔子懷胎。師乃云：兔子懷胎，蚌含明月，乘時正在中秋節，一顆明珠轉玉盤，徹底無瑕光皎潔。檀越請上堂。紅日三竿高枕處，黃粮一鉢飽齋時。分明千聖排肩立，不肯承當過在誰。人人是佛，眾生日用不知，各各圓成幾箇。閙中瞥地，只為迷己逐物，執妄為真。從來蹭蹬覺虗行，多年枉作風塵客。致使家中至寶拋離向五蘊山頭，衣下明珠流落在三

Occurrences.Kwic: 入涅槃。白雲深處不曾居，豈肯將身伴草廬，嘗到洛陽花社裏，笑看潘閬倒騎驢。法身。昨夜露柱喫一跌，曉來燈籠痛不徹，須彌控訴妙高王，直至於今笑不歇。涅槃四生。生生。春林花茂艷陽天，李白桃紅在處妍，野老昇平無活計，村歌社舞樂堯年。不生生。澄澄虛碧鎖寒空，湛湛秋光景愈溶，莫謂玉人沉夜永，等閒歌舞月明中。生不生。花開花卸本無情，雲去雲來孰謂真，大用繁興元戀朕，縱橫那復有纖塵。不生不生。木人不打新羅鼓，石女停篙拄銕船，折角泥牛吞卻月，三更紅日黑漫漫。般若無知，無所不知。懷胎石女不梳頭，古鏡塵埋獨倚樓，卻笑嬋娟無禁拒，年來年去下滄洲。黃龍三關。我手何似佛手，拈起須彌倒走，若是獅子之兒，定不落人窠臼。我腳何似驢腳，放開頂門一著，可憐眼內無筋，往往被人穿卻。人人有箇生緣，玄沙不出飛猿，未動腳跟薦得，已遭紅線抽牽。正偏五位。正中偏，古殿光騰未兆前，鳥雞啄破無明卵，炤徹東方萬八千。偏中正，法法頭頭無少剩，森羅萬象絕纖塵，誰能更把空王令。正中來，龜毛兔角謾安排，出沒本能該世界，豈同諸類混塵埃。兼中至，妙用無私靡

Senses.Explanation: ‘Wisdom does not grasp at knowing, yet nothing is left unknown’ is a compact contrast about prajna. The surviving sayings prevent both an ignorant reading of the first half and an inflated claim of fact possession from the second. Yezhu tells a student that the line's ‘without knowing’ is not ignorance and recalls a Fayan exchange where not knowing is closer. Cishou extends the pair to seeing, then asks how wisdom's body and use appear in an old case. A verse in Hanyue's collection appears under this heading and answers with clouds and spring. Yuanjie's collection has another verse under the same heading, using a pregnant stone woman and a dimmed old mirror.

Senses.Explanation: A paste cake is a prepared flour cake that becomes a compact answer and case object. Yunmen Wenyan answers the public request for talk beyond buddhas and ancestors with ‘paste cake’; Jiashan Shanhui holds one up to Luopu while pressing the claim that the many kinds do not leave this one. Later masters quote, verse, and criticize those uses, so the food remains concrete even when it is wielded in an interview.
